articles.title: Murphy Oil Re-Enters Cameroon
articles.description: Cameroon awarded Murphy Oil four production sharing contracts, marking the company's re-entry into the Central African country after exiting a decade ago.

articles.title: USA Oil, Gas Workforce Hits Lowest Figure So Far in 2026
articles.description: The number of employees in the oil and gas extraction industry hit its lowest figure so far this year, data on the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics website showed.

articles.title: Aramco, PIF Close HUMAIN AI Deal
articles.description: The deal involves approximately $2.6 billion in cash contributions in 2026 from Aramco to HUMAIN, in addition to AI, compute, and digital assets.

articles.title: Eni Plans Nearly $15B Gross Investment in UK through 2030
articles.description: Eni unveiled plans for around GBP 11 billion in 'gross investments' in the United Kingdom between 2026 and 2030, focused on lower-carbon projects.

articles.title: SLB wins Vår Energi integrated drilling services deal on NCS
articles.description: Energy technology company SLB has been selected by Vår Energi as the main supplier of integrated drilling services for the Transocean Barents and Deepsea Bergen rigs operating on the Norwegian Continental Shelf (NCS).

articles.title: Reliance plans $4.6bn investment in Andhra Pradesh coal-to-gas project
articles.description: Indian multinational conglomerate Reliance Industries has outlined plans to invest approximately Rs430bn ($4.57bn) in a facility to transform underground coal into gas in Andhra Pradesh, India, according to a government memorandum reviewed by Reuters.

articles.title: IEA Sees Oil Surplus for First Time in Iran War
articles.description: 'The oil market is showing tentative signs of rebalancing, with global oil supplies surpassing demand for the first time since the outbreak of the war in Iran'.

articles.title: Iran Rules Out Return of UN Nuclear Inspectors as U.S. War Talks Stall
articles.description: Iran continues to divert attempts by the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) to access and verify the Iranian stockpile of enriched uranium and rules out any engagement with the UN’s agency’s inspectors amid the standoff in the war with the U.S. “It is more than a year since the agency lost continuity of knowledge in relation to the previously declared inventories of highly-enriched uranium,” IAEA Director General Rafael Mariano Grossi wrote in a restricted report, which was circulated in Vienna on Friday and was seen…

articles.title: How Global Energy Markets Survived Eight Months of Iran War Disruptions
articles.description: Six months ago, I wrote that Americans were experiencing the Iran war primarily through higher prices, while much of the rest of the world was confronting something more serious: actual shortages of fuel and other critical products. In “The U.S. Feels Higher Prices While The World Is Facing Fuel Shortages,” I highlighted several pressure points created by the disruption of traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. India was struggling to secure liquefied petroleum gas, or LPG, fertilizer markets were tightening, Europe faced potential…

articles.title: Pakistan Scrambles for LNG as Winter Gas Crisis Deepens
articles.description: State-owned Pakistan LNG Limited (PLL) has issued a tender to purchase two LNG cargoes from international suppliers for delivery in mid-December and early January, Business Recorder reports, citing a tender notice. Winning bidders in the tender are expected to deliver the LNG cargoes on a delivered ex-ship (DES) basis at Port Qasim, one in the December 14-16 window, and the other between January 9 and 11, 2027. The new tender is a re-issue of a previous one, in which Pakistan had rejected bids from two suppliers, who had quoted prices of between…

articles.title: ExxonMobil to invest $12.5bn in Longtail development offshore Guyana
articles.description: ExxonMobil, through its subsidiary ExxonMobil Guyana, has reached a final investment decision (FID) to move forward with the development of the Longtail field, located offshore Guyana.

articles.title: Iran Says Gas Tanker Hit Mine in Strait of Hormuz
articles.description: A tanker carrying liquefied gas hit a mine and suffered an explosion on Friday while attempting to transit the Strait of Hormuz via a route not authorized by Iran, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy said. The vessel was using an “unauthorised and dangerous route” in the Strait of Hormuz, according to Iran’s state media cited by Reuters. The attacks on vessels carrying energy products through the Strait of Hormuz have intensified in the past month, with Iran reporting incidents nearly every day. On Thursday,…

articles.title: Nvidia Spy Scandal Threatens the Gulf’s AI Ambitions
articles.description: Politics, Geopolitics & Conflict A car bomb killed the chief navigator of Russia’s St. Petersburg-based 6th Guards Air and Air Defence Forces Army on Thursday morning, a day after Ukrainian drones set an oil terminal at Ust-Luga on fire and forced flight restrictions at St. Petersburg’s Pulkovo airport. The colonel’s car exploded about 300 meters from his apartment in Shushary, the same suburb where a car bomb killed a helicopter regiment officer in August. Investigators believe a 31-year-old local planted the device overnight…

articles.title: Why Falling Oil Prices Won't Save America From Inflation
articles.description: Don’t look to falling oil prices to stave off inflation now. Brent is down from above $100 to the low $90s; Saudi Arabia pumped 10.56 million barrels a day in October, back at pre-war levels and above its quota, and gasoline just posted its steepest one-day drop in 18 years. Consumer prices still rose an estimated 4% from a year earlier in October, with pump prices slightly lower, up from 3.7% in September, and core prices rose 0.3% in a single month. Expect the Fed to hike in December, but markets have already priced this in. October’s…

articles.title: WTI Stages Sharp Comeback as Middle East Supply Risks Intensify
articles.description: December WTI crude oil futures are lower for the week, but the market has recovered a good portion of its early loss. The contract opened at $90.83, broke to $83.88, then rallied back to $88.20. At that price, WTI is down $2.63 for the week, or 2.90%. Traders took war premium out of crude after President Trump played down the possibility of new U.S. strikes on Iran. Higher Saudi production and a large build in U.S. inventories gave sellers more to work with. But attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure and continued threats to shipping brought buyers…

articles.title: Asian Refiners Turn Back to Gulf Oil Despite War Risks
articles.description: Asia’s refiners are back to buying Middle Eastern oil as flows through the Strait of Hormuz rise, freight rates ease from record highs, and Gulf producers are offering their crude at discounts to regional benchmarks. Chinese, Japanese, and Thai oil refiners are increasingly preferring cargoes from the Middle East in recent weeks, even those that need to transit the Strait of Hormuz, traders with knowledge of the matter told Bloomberg on Friday. Refiners in the world’s top crude oil-importing region are buying greater volumes…

articles.title: India Seeks Private Investors for $910 Million Oil Reserve
articles.description: India is looking for private investors to build and operate the nation’s largest strategic petroleum reserve site, which will boost India’s SPR capacity by 80% and cost an estimated $910 million, local media reported on Friday, citing tender documents. The proposed SPR site will be located at Chandikhol in the eastern Indian state of Odisha on the Bay of Bengal, and will be capable of holding up to 4 million tons of crude oil. The Indian government is offering a grant of $546 million (51.4 billion Indian rupees) to support private…

articles.title: Asian Airlines Face a $148-a-Barrel Fuel Gamble
articles.description: Asian airlines are facing expiring jet fuel hedge contracts and need to make a choice about whether to hedge at exorbitant prices or risk them going even higher without a hedge. Citing industry executives, Reuters reported today that jet fuel prices in Asia are currently about 75% higher than they were before the war in the Middle East started, and that the chance of that changing dramatically in the observable future appears to be slim. “Our view is that we are facing a new normal where the fuel price is there to stay at the levels that…

articles.title: Oil Prices Head for Second Weekly Loss Despite Fresh Middle East Attacks
articles.description: Crude oil prices were on course to book their second week of losses today, after two consecutive days of gains on news from the Middle East. At the time of writing, Brent crude was trading at $95.87 per barrel, with West Texas Intermediate at $88.49 per barrel. These price levels are a sharp decline from the peaks hit in mid-October, but are still significantly higher than what Brent crude and WTI traded at in February, before the war started. Signals about that war remain mixed. There appears to be only a moderate risk of serious escalation, but…

articles.title: Oil Rises as Trump Dims Iran Deal Hopes
articles.description: Oil prices rose more than 3% as Trump's comments dampened hopes for a diplomatic breakthrough with Iran.

articles.title: VEN Sends First Oil Gear in Years to USA for Repairs
articles.description: Venezuela is sending state-owned oil equipment to the U.S. for repairs for the first time in more than a decade.

articles.title: Rare Earth Wars: U.S. General Sounds Alarm Over China's Military Leverage
articles.description: On November 3, retired four-star General Jack Keane, the Army's former Vice Chief of Staff, put a warning on the record: China "has made clear it is prepared to use [America’s] dependence as leverage." The dependence he's talking about is America's reliance on Chinese rare earths. And he didn't say it from a cable news set. He said it as a director of REalloys [NASDAQ: ALOY], the company the Army recently selected for exclusive negotiations to build a plant to process dysprosium and terbium on one of its own military bases. And the timing…

articles.title: Oil Prices Squeezed Between Peace Hopes and Iran Escalation Risk
articles.description: Oil prices have crashed about 20% from the late-October peak of $118 per barrel, weighed down by hopes of sustainable de-escalation in the Middle East and the Russia-Ukraine war. For months, traders and hedge funds have often bet on a resolution of the conflicts, only to reactivate buying when talks fall apart. As U.S.-mediated talks between Ukraine and Russia are underway, there are no signs of a breakthrough in either the conflict in Europe or the U.S.-Iran standoff, despite messaging via Qatar. Oil prices have slipped as crude oil flows from…

articles.title: Venezuela Ends 19-Year Power Monopoly, With Oil Fields First in Line
articles.description: Venezuela is opening up its electricity sector to private capital for the first time since Hugo Chávez nationalized it in 2007, in a reform passed this week primarily to benefit oil producers and large businesses that can afford euro-pegged tariffs, while the state keeps the hydroelectric dams and main transmission lines that supply most households living with daily blackouts. The law, which the National Assembly passed unanimously on Tuesday, lets oil producers build power plants for their own fields without state authorization, as long…
